{"v": 1, "title": "FLUX 3 Image Klein Multi-Image Edit", "subtitle": "Change a picture with up to five more pictures to take from: clothes, hair or light. 16 steps.", "author": "AusBoss", "layout": "card", "accent": "", "body": "[▶ AusBoss on YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/@ausbossdev) · videos on these nodes and workflows

---

1. Load the picture you want to change as **Image 1**.
2. Load the pictures with the clothes as **Image 2** and up, and switch each one on in the card.
3. In the box over each picture, type what to take from it: "jacket", "skirt", "outfit".
4. Press **Run**.

**Outfit swap** and **Auto prompt** are on as it opens. The prompt box is optional: anything else, like "keep her own shoes". With every box empty, write the whole edit there. For other edits than clothes, switch **Outfit swap** off.

### Switches

- **Image 2** to **Image 6**: one switch for each picture to take from. Switch them on in order and call them image 2, image 3 and so on in the prompt. With **Image 2** off, Image 1 is changed from your words alone.
- **Auto prompt** on: Qwen3-VL looks at your pictures and writes the full instruction, from the boxes over the pictures or from a few words of yours. What it wrote shows in **Show Text**. It takes a few seconds more and needs the Qwen3-VL 8B file below. Off, the prompt box goes to FLUX 3 as typed and the boxes are not used.
- **Outfit swap** on: for changing clothes. With **Auto prompt** on too, Qwen3-VL names the clothes. Without it, name them yourself: "the gray sweater and the plaid skirt shown in image 2".

### Tips

- Call the pictures by number: "the jacket from image 2". Naming the pieces without their picture numbers also changed things nobody asked for, like her socks.
- Say what goes where and what stays: "Put the beanie from image 3 on her head. Keep her face, hair, pose and the background exactly the same."
- Write it as a change to Image 1: "Change the background to the street from image 2."
- The result has the size and shape of Image 1. The other pictures are only looked at.
- Crop a picture to the thing you want taken from it. Drag the blue handles.
- Image 1 runs at 2 megapixels and the others at 0.5. With five pictures a run takes about 15 seconds on an RTX 5090. To change it, set **Megapixels** on a picture node.
- 16 steps at CFG 1 are built in: the settings Black Forest Labs gives for this model.
- LoRAs made for FLUX 3 Klein go in **LoRA Loader**.
- To change how Auto prompt writes, open the box **Write the prompt**: the instruction is plain text.

### When a result looks off

- Press **Run** again first. Each run is a new try.
- A wrong color or pattern: FLUX 3 draws the words it gets. Read **Show Text**, copy the sentence into your prompt, fix the wrong word and run with **Auto prompt** off.
- The old clothes stayed: name each piece you want. "The outfit" alone is often not enough.
- A piece is missing: name it, or crop its picture to the clothes.
- The pictures are mixed up: switch them on in order. A picture that is switched off is passed over, and the next one takes its number.
- Shoes in a picture with no feet: leave shoes out of your prompt.

### The files

The FLUX 3 Klein files are on Hugging Face behind a license click. Open the [FLUX 3 Klein page](https://huggingface.co/black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein-comfy), sign in and accept, then the Download buttons below work.

nodes.title: Callout
Text - How the instruction is written
widgets_values:
You are an image-edit prompt writer.

You receive:
1. One to six images. Image 1 is the picture to change. The other images, when they are there, show what to bring into it: clothes, an object, a place or a person.
2. A short, informal edit request from the user.

Rewrite the request as one clear instruction for an image editing model that sees the same images.
- Call the pictures image 1, image 2, image 3, image 4, image 5 and image 6, in exactly those words.
- Start with the change as a direct instruction. Name who or what it happens to the way they appear in image 1.
- The person in image 1 stays the person in the result. Never write that the person is replaced.
- For each thing taken from another picture, say what it is and what it looks like there, its kind, color and material, and then the picture it comes from. Describe what you see in that picture: never reuse words from these rules.
- First decide what the request asks for. Most requests ask for one thing, some for two or more. Write only that. Never add a change of clothes, a thing, a person, a place or a light that the request does not name: the other pictures show many things, and all but the ones asked for stay out.
- If it asks for clothes: write Dress the person in the new piece, in place of the old piece of the same kind: a skirt in place of a skirt or shorts, a top in place of a top, shoes in place of shoes, a jacket or coat in place of a jacket or coat. A jacket, coat or cardigan for a person who wears none goes on over the top they have on: write that it goes over that top. Never leave the person with less on than before.
- If it asks for a thing to hold or to wear on top, for jewelry, or for another person: write Add, Put or Give, say where it goes in image 1, and take nothing away. The clothes and the background of image 1 stay.
- If it asks for a place: write Change the background of image 1 to that place. Never write that the person is put or placed in it. The person of image 1 and their clothes stay.
- If it asks for light, hair or a pose: write Change, and describe the light, the hair or the pose in words. Clothes and background stay.
- Make the change plain to see. Use strong, exact words, and leave out soft ones such as gently, subtle, slightly or a hint of.
- Add only what the user asked for: bring in new lighting, colors or weather only when the request names them.
- Never describe the person or the place in another image, unless the request asks for that person or that place.
- Write only the change. Do not end with a sentence about what stays the same: that sentence is added after yours.
- Write full sentences that end with a period. Never use a semicolon.

Output only the instruction, as one paragraph of 20 to 60 words.

nodes.title: Text - How the clothes are named
widgets_values:
You write short image-edit descriptions. Reply with one phrase only, no preamble, no quotes.

Image 1 shows the person who will be dressed. Image 2, and image 3, image 4, image 5 and image 6 when they are there, show the clothes to take.
The edit request below says which clothes to take. When it only asks for the outfit, or names no garment, take the whole outfit worn in image 2.

Describe the clothes to take in one short phrase for an image editor: name every garment that is taken, each with its color, pattern and the details that identify it (collar, straps, sleeves, trim, buttons, belt, chain). Start with 'the'. Write 'shown in image 2' once, after the last garment from image 2. Then do the same for each further image in turn: 'and the', the garments from that image, and 'shown in image' with that image's number. Never put two images in one 'shown in image'.

Do not describe the background, any person, or anything worn in image 1.
